title: Move a layer from A to B, grow it, shrink it, fade it, Photoshop-style
goal: The user wants Photoshop-style motion in video: move a text or picture layer from one place to another, grow it, shrink it, turn it and fade it by dragging it on the canvas at two moments. The keys show on its track and can be dragged.
notes:
Intake detail (the goal as first filed, moved here by triage 2026-09-23): The user wants Photoshop blended into video: 'create text layers, animate them from place a to b, make transitions, grow/shrink elements'. Target: the user's mocks (docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html, video-shell.html, comp-video.html and the page named here) at their fidelity; runner-prompt rules on default config, side-by-side with the mock, labels-not-explanations and right-click apply. Ask throughout: would a Premiere editor get this, and is it easier here?

Filed from the 2026-09-23 video audit in the intake window.
acceptance: Press T over the video, type: the text is a layer on a titles track with an in and an out you drag

Move the playhead, drag or resize any layer on the canvas: with keyframing armed (a diamond on the track header, as Premiere's stopwatch) that makes a key; position, scale, rotation and opacity animate between keys
Keys show on the layer's track as diamonds you can drag, right-click for easing (Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In and Out) and delete
In and Out presets for titles (fade, slide, pop, scale) from the right-click menu
A walk makes a title fly in from the left, grow, and fade out, at Next defaults

log.note: triage 2026-09-23: goal rewritten in plain language, the old one kept at the top of notes

manager 2026-09-23 06:10: every-value-in-the-panel-has-a-key-diamond is sequenced before this and builds the keying itself (panel diamonds, and a change on the canvas at another moment adds a key). This task then draws those keys on the layer's track in the new timeline, adds easing from right-click and the In and Out presets. Build on its keys, do not add a second arming control.

video-shell.html was deleted on 2026-09-23 (task the-video-mocks-are-the-user-s-again-and-d18-is): it was the loop's own study arguing against tracks. The target is now pages/video.html, the video-*.html walkthroughs and comp-video.html, restored as the user drew them, plus UX-PATTERNS D18 (rewritten: a document with time has tracks). Where this task mentions video-shell, read video.html.

Adversarial pre-build: (1) keys already exist (panel diamonds, canvas drags fold into keys, commit 7d42ef58); what is missing is seeing them on the timeline, moving them, easing them and one-click title animations. (2) The mock (comp-video.html .kfm, video-kit css) draws key marks on a clip as READ-ONLY, the user's acceptance here asks for diamonds you drag and right-click: building the acceptance (the user's own words, newer), listing it as a mock difference in the audit. (3) Easing: the mock's key card says the curve LEAVING a key; a Premiere editor's right-click on a key says Ease In = slow arriving, Ease Out = slow leaving, and it works on the last key too. Building Premiere's meaning, since the acceptance names Premiere's four items; stored per key, a segment eases where either of its keys says so, and a motion nobody has eased plays exactly as it does today. (4) A clip bar shows one diamond per MOMENT (the union of every keyed value there), as the mock's .kfm does; dragging or easing it acts on every value keyed at that moment. (5) The acceptance's 'diamond on the track header to arm keying' conflicts with the manager's note (do not add a second arming control): the panel diamond stays the one stopwatch, the header gets nothing. (6) Presets write ordinary keys (Animate In / Animate Out on the clip's and the layer's right-click menu), so everything they make is draggable and easable, and Undo takes one away in one step. (7) Walks cannot drag a SwiftUI bar with a real pointer (tracks task notes), so the key drag is driven through EditorState in walks; the gesture is exercised by hand in the probe.

Built: core ClipKeys.swift (clipKeyMarks, moveClipKeys, easeClipKeys, removeClipKeys, animateIn/animateOut with Fade/Slide/Pop/Scale) + per-key KeyEase on LayerMotion (a motion nobody eased plays byte-for-byte as before), tested first in ClipKeyMarksTests (21). A title's own track is now named Title (mock), V numbers are for everything else; DocumentTracks/ClipLanding tests updated. App: diamonds on every clip in ClipPiecesBar (drag with playhead snap and a time readout, click = playhead to key, right-click = Linear/Ease In/Ease Out/Ease In and Out, Go to Key, Delete Key), Animate In/Out on the clip's and the canvas's right-click (EditorState+ClipKeys.swift). Fixed on the way: a title's clip menu offered Speed, which means nothing without media (TitleTime's own rule); it now needs media behind it. Walk actions clipKeyAtPlayheadLater and videoStepQuarterSecond added.
